newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strikes set at three French oil plants on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Strikes set at three French oil plants on Tuesday.

text.p: Workers have called one-day strikes for Tuesday at three French oil refineries and a go-slow will disrupt a fourth in a protest about jobs, union officials said on Monday. Further action is planned later in the week.

Unions said they had given notice of strikes on Tuesday at the 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) BP refinery at Lavera, the 127,000 bpd La Mede refinery run by Total and Royal Dutch/Shell's 128,000 bpd Berre refinery, where workers plan to extend a strike begun on Monday.
Shell's Petit Couronne refinery in north France will operate at the minimum safe rate on Tuesday, union officials said.
The three refineries where strikes are scheduled on Tuesday are all near Marseille on the Mediterranean coast.
Tuesay's programme of strikes, covering some 450,000 barrels per day (bpd) or a quarter of French capacity, falls short of plans for a nationwide oil strike to protest about industry job cuts.
But an official at the CFDT union, France's largest, said it would herald some action at other plants later in the week.
Current plans include a slowdown at Mobil's 70,000 bpd lubricants refinery at Gravenchon in northern France between Wednesday and Friday, he said.
Workers at the nearby Esso Port Jerome refinery plan a full strike from Thursday to Saturday, he said.
France's largest oil firm Elf Aquitaine appeared to be spared significant new disruption as it recovered from a crippling nine-day strike which ended on Friday.
Its three French refineries are unlikely to take part in new strikes so soon after the last protest, union officials said.
But one said workers there may lend support through mass meetings that might slow efforts to get things back to normal.
Elf said earlier its plants were getting back to normal.
Unions said other planned action included demonstrations at Shell's French oil industry research centre.
Workers at Shell's Berre refinery went on strike early on Monday, halting deliveries out of the plant, shutting some petrochemical units and slowing down refinery distillation.
Their strike, originally called for 24 hours, is now set to be extended throughout Tuesday, union officials said.
Unions are campaigning against stringent cost cuts in the refining sector which they say will push at least 1,500 people out of work in France and have no economic justification.
Oil companies say belt-tightening is necessary to confront fierce competition from supermarkets in petrol retailing and a glut of spare capacity in European refining.
